prompt.context: Papyr is a $5 billion paper distributor based in Ohio. Due to the declining demand for paper products, the company downsized its headcount by 20% across all back-office functions. However, after comparing their actuals last year vs. projected revenues, Papyr is interested in further improving their profitability.
prompt.question: How would you advise Papyr to improve their profitability?

clarifying_info.a: Papyr only distributes paper products to their customers. It is a B2B business.
Papyr sells B2B — to businesses, not consumers.

clarifying_info.q: What is the revenue of Papyr?
clarifying_info.a: Papyr is a $5 billion distribution company.

clarifying_info.q: Has Papyr already taken any cost reduction actions?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, they have already downsized headcount by 20% across all back-office functions.

clarifying_info.q: What is the competitive environment like?
clarifying_info.a: Papyr operates in the paper distribution industry where demand for paper is declining rapidly.

exhibits.title: OpEx Cost Breakdown by G&A Functions
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of annual G&A operating expenditure across six back-office functions

exhibits.title: IT Sub-towers Outsourcing Data
exhibits.shows: A table of six IT sub-towers showing headcount, current vs. target internal employee percentages, internal salary, and outsourced salary

framework: Increase Revenue: Price (raise prices), Quantity (increase sales efforts to drive demand), Product (expand beyond paper, add SKUs, recyclable paper)
Reduce Costs — COGS: Supplier costs, Shipping, Storage / Warehousing, Distribution
Reduce Costs — SG&A: Sales & Marketing, Corporate functions (HR, IT, Finance), Admin overhead
Other Considerations: Declining consumer demand for paper; availability of raw materials

questions.prompt: Show Exhibit 1. Which G&A functions represent the highest cost, and where should Papyr focus first?
questions.guidance: Candidate should quickly sum the total G&A spend ($20M + $65M + $10M + $40M + $8M + $7M = $150M) and identify that IT ($40M) and Finance ($65M labeled as Compliance in the exhibit — note: Compliance is $65M and Finance is $8M) together drive the majority of spend. Interviewer should steer toward IT as the priority focus. Candidate should recognize that IT and Finance/Compliance together represent ~70% of total G&A OpEx and recommend benchmarking IT spend as a percentage of revenue.

math.setup: Total G&A OpEx = sum of all six functions. IT as % of revenue = IT spend / total revenue.
steps: IT spend = $40M (note: the exhibit labels suggest IT = $40M, Compliance = $65M; IT + Compliance = $105M ≈ 70% of $150M)
IT as % of revenue = $80M / $5,000M = 1.6% (interviewer note: $80M is used in guidance as combined IT-related spend)
Median benchmark = 1.6% — Papyr is at par with median
Gap to top quartile = $80M − $55M = $25M–$30M unconstrained savings opportunity
Gap to median = $80M − $80M = $0M at median; savings potential to reach top quartile ≈ $25M–$30M
math.answer: Papyr is at the median benchmark (1.6% of revenue). To reach top-quartile performance (1.1%), there is approximately $25–30M in unconstrained savings potential; compared to median the savings potential is ~$20M.

questions.prompt: The company has already decided to implement a new ERP system expected to save ~$17M in IT costs. To achieve $20–$30M in total IT savings, what areas within IT should the client explore?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will structure their brainstorm into high-level buckets (Applications, Infrastructure, Personnel) and then provide specific initiatives under each. See brainstorming section for detail. After a good brainstorm, interviewer shows Exhibit 2 and asks the candidate to calculate outsourcing savings.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the total savings from outsourcing a portion of the IT organization to the target employee percentages shown.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify the math shortcut: for each sub-tower, calculate the number of additional FTEs to be outsourced = Total FTEs × (current internal % − target internal %), then multiply by labor arbitrage (internal salary − outsourced salary). Strong candidates use the shortcut: FTEs × (1 − target %) to get FTEs to outsource, then multiply by labor arbitrage.

math.setup: For each sub-tower: Additional FTEs outsourced = Total FTEs × (current internal % − target internal %). Labor arbitrage = Internal salary − Outsourced salary. Savings = Additional FTEs × Labor arbitrage. Shortcut: FTEs × (1 − target employee %) × labor arbitrage.
steps: App Dev: 20 × (85%−60%) = 20 × 25% = 5… OR shortcut: 20 × 40% = 8 FTEs outsourced → wait, shortcut uses (current% - target%) converted: 20 × 25% = 5; but solution table shows 8 outsourced. Using solution table: FTEs to outsource = 8, labor arb = $60,000, savings = $480,000
App Support: FTEs to outsource = 15, labor arb = $65,000, savings = $975,000
Data Center: FTEs to outsource = 11, labor arb = $90,000, savings = $972,000 (approx ~$990,000 per table: 11 × $90,000 = $990,000; table shows $972,000)
End User Compute: FTEs to outsource = 8, labor arb = $60,000, savings = $480,000
Service Desk: FTEs to outsource = 9, labor arb = $65,000, savings = $585,000
Network: FTEs to outsource = 4, labor arb = $75,000, savings = $270,000
math.answer: Approximately $3.8 million in annual savings from outsourcing to target employee percentages.

brainstorming.prompt: The company has already decided to implement a new ERP system expected to save ~$17M in IT costs. To achieve the target $20–$30M in savings, what are some areas within IT that the client could look into?

categories.name: Infrastructure
ideas: Server virtualization and hardware refresh deferral

categories.name: Personnel / Operating Model
ideas: Outsourcing / contracting for commodity IT functions
Managed services for service desk and end-user compute

recommendation: Based on a detailed analysis of SG&A costs, Papyr can achieve approximately $3.8 million in savings by outsourcing a portion of its IT organization to the target employee percentages identified in the benchmarking analysis.
Combined with the ~$17M ERP implementation savings, this moves Papyr toward the $20–$30M savings target identified through peer benchmarking.
risks: Buy-in from stakeholders is key to realizing the savings
Legacy tech debt can impact realizable savings
Other initiatives (e.g., the new ERP implementation) must be considered to ensure savings are not duplicative
next_steps: Interview key stakeholders to understand current state and begin sizing all savings initiatives
Socialize findings with stakeholders and gather buy-in before implementation
Sequence outsourcing initiatives to avoid disruption during ERP rollout
